title: Precision economics calculator — 4-bit / FP8 / INT8 sensitivity workbook
content:
Purpose and audience:
This is a working workbook for the Optimize team to compare precision modes (INT8, FP8, 4-bit) across three axes: unit cost, model output quality, and end-to-end latency. Intended readers: product-optimize, serving-runtime, and solutions-eng. Goal is to produce a compact decision rubric and a small spreadsheet template we can hand to SREs and Solutions for rapid PoCs.

Summary (one-sentence):
A lightweight calculator and heuristics for selecting precision profiles based on target SLOs (latency), budget (cost per 1M tokens), and allowable quality degradation (task metric delta).

Assumptions and definitions (keep these updated in the sheet):
- "Unit" = 1M generated tokens.
- Cost model uses GPU-hour pricing (on-prem internal rate or cloud reserved rate) + proportional infra overhead (network, storage).
- Quality delta measured against baseline FP16/FP32 using task-specific metric (e.g., Exact Match for QA, ROUGE for summarization, or human A/B % pref).
- Latency measured p50/p95 of end-to-end request (including de/serialization, model inference, KV/prefix cache hit effects).
- Throughput measured in effective tokens/sec perGPU for steady-state streaming.
- Safety guardrail: if quality drop > X% (configurable), automatically block auto-upgrade.

Spreadsheet template (columns we used in prototype workbook):
- precision (string): INT8 | FP8 | 4-bit | baseline
- model_variant (string): e.g., gpt-3.1-large-q8 | gpt-3.1-large-fp8
- seq_len_profile (string): short (<=128) | med (128-1024) | long (>1024)
- batch_size (int)
- gpu_type (string): A100-80GB, H100, etc.
- mem_use_gb (float)
- tokens_per_sec (float)  # measured perf for this precision & batch
- latency_p95_ms (float)
- cost_per_hour_usd (float)  # GPU incremental cost
- infra_overhead_pct (float)  # estimated 0-30%
- unit_cost_per_1M_usd (formula)  # see formula notes below
- quality_metric_base (float)  # baseline metric (e.g., ROUGE)
- quality_metric_quant (float)  # metric after quant
- quality_delta_pct (float)  # (quant - base)/base * 100
- recommended_flag (string)  # prefer/intended/fallback/do-not-use
- notes (string)  # quick observations (e.g., hallucination tendency, kernel mismatch)

Key formulas (as plain-text so SREs can paste into sheets):
- tokens_per_hour = tokens_per_sec * 3600
- effective_gpu_hours_per_1M_tokens = 1_000_000 / tokens_per_hour
- unit_cost_per_1M_usd = effective_gpu_hours_per_1M_tokens * (cost_per_hour_usd * (1 + infra_overhead_pct/100))
- quality_delta_pct = (quality_metric_quant - quality_metric_base) / max(0.0001, quality_metric_base) * 100

Example prototype numbers (measured on H100, sequence med, batch 4) — replace with lab numbers for each model:
- baseline FP16: tokens_per_sec=2500, latency_p95_ms=220, cost_per_hour_usd=3.20, unit_cost_per_1M_usd ≈ 1.15, quality_delta_pct=0
- INT8: tokens_per_sec=3600, latency_p95_ms=170, cost_per_hour_usd=3.20, infra_overhead_pct=10, unit_cost_per_1M_usd ≈ 0.78, quality_delta_pct=-0.6 -> notes: small perf win, often safe for chat/completion
- FP8: tokens_per_sec=4200, latency_p95_ms=150, cost_per_hour_usd=3.20, infra_overhead_pct=12, unit_cost_per_1M_usd ≈ 0.61, quality_delta_pct=-1.8 -> notes: good perf, occasional numeric instability on large context
- 4-bit (GPTQ-like): tokens_per_sec=4800, latency_p95_ms=140, cost_per_hour_usd=3.20, infra_overhead_pct=18, unit_cost_per_1M_usd ≈ 0.54, quality_delta_pct=-6.5 -> notes: requires per-layer re-tuning, sometimes degrades factuality

Heuristic decision rubric (starter rules to automate recommendations):
- If quality_delta_pct >= -1% and unit_cost_per_1M_usd reduction >= 25% => Recommend INT8 as primary upgrade.
- If quality_delta_pct between -1% and -4% and reduction >= 35% => FP8 is candidate; require canary with human eval and metric-based alerts.
- If quality_delta_pct < -4% or erratic eval signals => 4-bit only for non-critical offline workloads (embedding/rerank batch jobs) OR when combined with strong prefix caching & reranking.
- For low-latency SLOs (p95 budget <= 150ms), prefer FP8/4-bit only if measured p95 meets SLO and tail stability confirmed across benchmarks.

Rollout checklist for a precision change (can be automated into Console rollout):
- Create model-variant tag and record hash + quant config (bits, kernel, requant params).
- Run unit-quality eval suite (N=500 prompts for targeted task) -> record metric deltas.
- Canary deploy to 2% traffic for 48 hours; collect metric and human-annotation samples.
- If metric drops > configured threshold or human pref < 90% of baseline -> rollback.
- If metrics stable, ramp to 20% for 72 hours, then full rollout.
- Always enable automatic fallback to baseline variant on mem pressure or error rates > X.

Open questions / experiments to run (short to do list):
- Measure sequence-length sensitivity: create curves of quality_delta_pct vs seq_len for each precision and model family.
- Quantization-aware prompt-sensitivity: some prompts (math, numeric, code) degrade non-uniformly — measure per-prompt slice.
- Kernel warm-up cost for 4-bit: does first-request latency spike add enough tail risk to disqualify for low-traffic customers?
- Interaction with KV cache: confirm that increased tokens/sec from 4-bit actually reduces cost for short-turn conversations (cache hit dominated).

Notes to reviewers (informal):
- This doc is meant to seed a small shared sheet that will be our canonical sensitivity workbook. I intentionally kept the example numbers coarse — please paste in lab traces (perf logs + eval runs) and iterate.
- If you have prior FP8/4-bit PRs or test harnesses, drop links in linked_artifacts.

Next steps (owners):
- Diego: run sequence-length sweep for gp-large on H100 (deadline 2025-09-24).
- Priya: curate 3 prompt slices for human-eval (deadline 2025-09-21).
- Samir: prototype the sheet with the formulas above and expose an API to import perf traces (deadline 2025-09-26).

Quick decision cheat-sheet (for product managers):
- If unit-cost savings < 20% -> don’t change precision unless latency benefits are required.
- If quality drop > 3% -> do not auto-rollout; escalate to applied-ml for micro-tuning.
- Prefer INT8 for conservative upgrades, FP8 for aggressive cost-first apps, 4-bit only for batched offline or heavily cached endpoints.

Raw experiment links / scratch notes:
- kernel bench: /mnt/lab/bench/2025-08-kernels-h100.log
- eval run 2025-09-01: github:repo/actions/runs/1223

-- end of workbook draft --

(Notes to self: convert the header to a small sheet and add an automatic "recommended_flag" computed column. Also add a chart: X-axis=unit_cost_per_1M_usd, Y-axis=quality_delta_pct, point size=latency_p95_ms.)
